title: Jefferson's Code No. 11 (the Barclay-Lamb code), coded passages of Barclay, Carmichael, Short and Jefferson, 1786-1791 (catalogue 483)

steps.what: Founders Online search 'Code No. 11': 18 documents 1786-1791; editors decoded from a partial reconstruction, no key found; no published key table found on the web or in cryptiana.
Founders text fetched through the built-in browser (WAF on plain HTTP); LoC item JSON gave master images on tile.loc.gov; 71 frames of 15 letters downloaded.
Two subagents transcribed the coded groups of TJ's copies (with clear sheets) and of Barclay's and Carmichael's letters with TJ's interlinear decodings.
Aligned the 40-group test line of TJ to Carmichael 15 Dec 1787 with the opening of his 14 Jun 1787 letter (PrC fetched); groups 14-40 fit; two misprints in the printed line found (519, 1097).
Segmentation solver (DP, then beam search keeping one value per repeated code) to cut each passage's plaintext among its groups; wrong seed values propagated; set aside.
attested_key.py: values only from TJ's interlinear decodings, clear-text sheets and printed pairs (key.tsv).

Checked each editors' conjecture against every occurrence of its groups: 1420 = de confirmed (De-ar Si-r); 1089 = -al (imperi-al); 495 = larg- in Barclay 1786 contradicts [sea]; 537 = u splits Kentuck[ians] differently; 1107 = t gives t-alk and Braban-t.

Barclay's undated ca. 3 Jul 1787 letter found filed under 12 Jun 1787 (007_0476-0481) by contact sheets of tile.loc.gov thumbnails; footnotes 1196.1084?.758.861.1307.626 and 265 (= Congress, confirmed).
TJ to Carmichael 11 Apr 1791 located by probing tile.loc.gov volumes (LoC item pages behind a bot check); 544 groups transcribed against the 'decyphered' sheet.
Short's despatches to Jay (NARA M34 roll 2, catalogue proxy): coded passages in Nos. 2, 5 and 6 (Oct 1789), the last not in the Founders hits; decodings in the State Department copy for Nos. 2 and 6.
make_reading.py: 1,868 of 1,917 counted groups carry a reading (97.4%), graded H/C/M/I.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1269 tokens, 509 types, en-modern order 4: reading -2.137 per letter; polyphonic: 25% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value. Verdict: not applicable.

validation.notes: polyphonic: 25% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The 348 values of key.tsv come from Jefferson's interlinear decodings of Barclay's and Carmichael's letters, his clear-text sheets for his own coded letters, and the decodings in the State Department copies of Short's despatches, all in the same correspondence; no key sheet survives.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.tsv: 1,917 counted code groups (37 quotations and struck groups excluded), 1,868 with a reading; groups with a '?' digit count as read only when a contemporary decoding or clear sheet fixes them

credits.note: Jefferson's interlinear decodings and clear-text sheets; the State Department clerk's decodings of Short's despatches

outcome.notes: Every coded passage already had a printed reading by the Jefferson Papers editors (prior solution, used for alignment); 216 groups rest only on it (grade M). The work adds the first value table of Code No. 11 and corrections: Barclay's footnote has six groups (The Pro-cur-e-r [General?]), [sea] at 495 is contradicted (495 = larg-), Kentuck[ians] splits as Ke-nt-u-[814], [tal]k is t-alk, and the printed 15 Dec 1787 test line has two misprints.

texts.label: Barclay to the American Commissioners, Madrid, 10 Apr 1786
texts.summary: Barclay reports from Madrid that Lamb's mission to Algiers has failed: no peace without a larger sum, and the Dey refuses to treat.

reading_review.note: The coded paragraph reads through as sentences (no peace without a larger sum; the Dey refuses to treat); Jefferson's interlinear decoding throughout.

texts.label: Barclay's coded footnotes, ca. 3 July 1787
texts.summary: Barclay's two coded footnotes name the Procureur général at Bordeaux (Dudon) as his adviser and Congress as the 'Particular Quarter' owing him money.

reading_review.note: the, e, r and Congress attested; three groups of Procurer General single occurrences.

texts.label: Jefferson to Barclay, 4 July 1787
texts.summary: Jefferson reports a conference on Barclay's arrest at Bordeaux with Montmorin's first secretary (Rayneval, by the editors' conjecture); the word the editors read as 'sea' is a group that means 'larg-' elsewhere in the code.

reading_review.note: de and Montmorin attested elsewhere; Rayneval, trouble single occurrences; 495 contradicts the printed 'sea'.

texts.label: Jefferson to Carmichael, Paris, 25 Sep 1787
texts.summary: Jefferson tells Carmichael of Smith's mission to Portugal, the failure to march into Holland, and a possible triple alliance of France, Austria and Russia.

reading_review.note: Coded phrases read as sense with Jefferson's clear sheet; the press copy digits are blotted but the sheet fixes the words.

texts.label: Jefferson to Adams, Paris, 28 Sep 1787, postscript
texts.summary: Jefferson's postscript to Adams that France is arranging with the two empires; written by mistake in the Barclay code, which Adams could not read.
texts.note: The LoC press copy is blotted past reading; no group could be transcribed. The reading file is the editors' text from the RC at the Massachusetts Historical Society, not checked here.

texts.label: Jefferson to Carmichael, Paris, 15 Dec 1787, test line
texts.summary: A test line: the opening of Jefferson's letter of 14 June 1787 put into code so that Carmichael could check his copy of the code.

reading_review.note: The test line reads as the opening of the 14 June 1787 letter; nine groups of the heading not split.

texts.label: Carmichael to Jefferson, Aranjuez, 8 May 1788
texts.summary: Carmichael explains that his cipher was wrong, has had no official news from America, and sketches Floridablanca's tactics against Eden.

reading_review.note: Coded runs read as sense between clear words; Carmichael's own garbling (official nature, 1081 nar) left as he wrote it.

texts.label: Carmichael to Jefferson, 29 May 1788
texts.summary: Carmichael on the Swedish armaments, the Russian minister's suspicion of England, and a British ship carrying war stores to the Turks.

reading_review.note: Coded words and phrases read as sense in the clear frame (Swedish armaments, a British ship for the Turks); a few groups Carmichael garbled.

texts.label: Jefferson to Carmichael, Paris, 3 Jun 1788
texts.summary: Jefferson on Littlepage, the survey for a canal across the isthmus of Panama, and the new French minister's quarrel over etiquette.

reading_review.note: Coded names and phrases (Littlepage, isthmus of Panama, the new French minister) read as sense from Jefferson's list.

texts.label: Carmichael to Jefferson, 5 Jun 1788
texts.summary: Carmichael on a Spanish ordinance meant to force a custom house on Biscay.

reading_review.note: Two coded phrases (a bugbear to compel them to admit a custom house; long held in view) read as sense.

texts.label: Carmichael to Jefferson, 24 Jul 1788
texts.summary: Carmichael on the 1360/1363 error in his cipher, Littlepage, and Campomanes and Ulloa on the Panama canal.

reading_review.note: Coded words are names and short phrases (Littlepage, Campomanes, Ulloa, a copy) that fit the clear text.

texts.label: Jefferson to Carmichael, Paris, 25 Dec 1788
texts.summary: Jefferson asks Carmichael what is being concerted between the Spanish court and the Kentucky settlers.

reading_review.note: The coded question about the Spanish court and the Kentucky settlers reads; three groups after 'Eden will be' and 814 open.

texts.label: Carmichael to Jefferson, 26 Jan 1789
texts.summary: Carmichael on a French agent sent to visit the American back settlements and on Gayoso, sent as governor of the Natchez.

reading_review.note: A continuous coded passage that reads as sentences (the French agent, Gayoso); two groups for 'secret' miscoded as 'sm'.

texts.label: Jefferson to Carmichael, Paris, 9 Aug 1789
texts.summary: Jefferson asks whether the provinces of Spain begin to talk of their rights, and reports Brabant in commotion.

reading_review.note: The provinces of Spain begin to talk of their rights? Brabant in commotion: reads, with two groups conjectural.

texts.label: Short to Jay, Paris, 9 Oct 1789 (No. 2)
texts.summary: Short on the October days: a party of the Duke of Orleans suspected of tampering with Lafayette's troops, and the royal family at the mercy of a mob.

reading_review.note: Syllable-by-syllable decoding from the copy reads as the sentences printed by the editors; dashes are groups the clerk left blank.

texts.label: Short to Jay, Paris, 25 Oct 1789 (No. 5)
texts.summary: Short on Mirabeau abandoning the Orleans party and seeking the ministry through Lafayette.

reading_review.note: No decoding in the copy: coded words aligned with the editors' text read as sense; 1612 for the Marquis unattested.

texts.label: Short to Jay, Paris, 28 Oct 1789 (No. 6)
texts.summary: Short mentions the ransom of the American prisoners at Algiers.

reading_review.note: Two coded words, ransom and prisoners, decoded in the copy.

texts.label: Jefferson to Carmichael, Philadelphia, 11 Apr 1791
texts.summary: Jefferson urges Carmichael to work for a joint front against the British navigation act and for the free navigation of the Mississippi.

reading_review.note: The long coded paragraph on the navigation act and the Mississippi reads through as sentences with the decyphered sheet.

prior.where: The Papers of Thomas Jefferson (Boyd et al., vols. 9-20, 1954-1982) and Papers of John Adams vol. 19, via Founders Online: every coded passage printed decoded from a partial reconstruction of Code No. 11, conjectures in brackets; no key table published.

human: Pasted the catalogue no. 483 task brief (from the project's solve page) into the session; no target-specific intervention.
